cards.statement: Administrators choose subnet regions and IP ranges for a custom mode VPC network.
cards.explanation: A custom mode VPC network starts with no subnets. Administrators create subnets in their chosen regions and assign their IP ranges.

cards.statement: A Shared VPC service project creates and owns the network subnets used by its application VMs.
cards.explanation: Shared VPC subnets belong to the host project. Authorized resources in attached service projects use those shared subnets.
cards.misconception: Service projects own the Shared VPC subnets they use.

cards.statement: VPC Network Peering can make a peer's other peers reachable through it.
cards.explanation: VPC Network Peering is non-transitive. Two networks peered with a common third network need their own connection to reach each other.
cards.misconception: Peering provides transit through a shared peer network.

cards.statement: An ingress VPC firewall rule can match the source IP range of incoming packets.
cards.explanation: An ingress VPC firewall rule can use CIDR source ranges to select incoming traffic before applying its allow or deny action.

cards.statement: A VPC firewall rule selects the target VM instances by matching their attached secure tag values.
cards.explanation: VPC firewall rules use network tags to select VMs. Secure tags select sources or targets in Cloud NGFW firewall policies.
cards.misconception: Secure tags target VMs in ordinary VPC firewall rules.

cards.statement: A VPC firewall rule can target VMs through their attached service account.
cards.explanation: A VPC firewall rule with target service accounts applies to VMs using a matching service account in the rule's network.

cards.statement: A VPC firewall rule can filter TCP traffic by its source port.
cards.explanation: VPC firewall rules can filter TCP traffic by destination port. Their protocol and port settings do not support source-port matching.
cards.misconception: VPC firewall rules support TCP source-port filters.

cards.statement: A hierarchical firewall policy associated with a folder automatically applies to its descendant projects.
cards.explanation: Associating a hierarchical firewall policy with a folder applies its enabled rules to applicable VMs in projects beneath that folder.

cards.statement: Cloud Router exchanges BGP routes over an HA VPN tunnel.
cards.explanation: Cloud Router establishes BGP sessions over HA VPN tunnels to exchange dynamic routes with a peer network.

cards.statement: Cloud Interconnect encrypts VLAN attachment traffic by default.
cards.explanation: Cloud Interconnect does not encrypt traffic by default. HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect is an option for encrypting VLAN attachment traffic.
cards.misconception: A private Interconnect connection provides encryption by default.

cards.statement: A regional internal Application Load Balancer sends traffic to backends in several regions.
cards.explanation: A regional internal Application Load Balancer uses backends in its own region. Cross-region internal mode supports backends across regions.
cards.misconception: Regional internal load balancing distributes requests to multi-region backends.

cards.statement: Premium Tier brings internet traffic onto Google's global network near the client.
cards.explanation: With Premium Tier, incoming traffic enters Google's network at a point of presence close to the sender and travels across Google's network toward the resource.

cards.statement: Config Connector reconciles Google Cloud resources declared as Kubernetes custom resources.
cards.explanation: Config Connector uses Kubernetes custom resource definitions and controllers to reconcile declared resources against Google Cloud APIs.

cards.statement: Fabric FAST supplies a Terraform reference design for a Google Cloud organization.
cards.explanation: Fabric FAST provides a reference organization design and Terraform implementation for foundational Google Cloud resources.

source.title: Terraform Examples and Modules for Google Cloud

cards.statement: Infrastructure Manager deploys Google Cloud resources from Deployment Manager templates.
cards.explanation: Infrastructure Manager deploys Terraform configurations. Deployment Manager used YAML configurations and Jinja or Python templates and has reached end of support.
cards.misconception: Infrastructure Manager accepts Deployment Manager templates as its deployment format.

cards.statement: Helm installs application charts stored in Artifact Registry into a GKE cluster.
cards.explanation: Helm can install a chart from an Artifact Registry repository as an application release in a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster.

source.title: Quickstart: Store Helm charts in Artifact Registry

cards.statement: Application Design Center lets developers add components while instantiating a standard template.
cards.explanation: When developers create an application from an Application Design Center standard template, they can configure its components but cannot add or remove them.
cards.misconception: Developers can change a standard template's component set when creating an application.
cards.volatilityNote: Application Design Center template capabilities continue to evolve.

cards.statement: Application Design Center can export Kubernetes manifests for its infrastructure designs.
cards.explanation: Application Design Center generates and exports Terraform files for templates and applications.
cards.misconception: Application Design Center exports Kubernetes manifests as its infrastructure code.
cards.volatilityNote: Application Design Center export formats and workflows can change.

cards.statement: Gemini CLI is available by default in Cloud Shell for terminal-based development work.
cards.explanation: Google Cloud provides Gemini CLI in Cloud Shell with no additional installation step.
cards.volatilityNote: Availability of AI tooling in Cloud Shell can change.

cards.statement: Gemini CLI receives a request quota separate from Gemini Code Assist agent mode.
cards.explanation: Gemini Code Assist edition quotas for Gemini CLI are shared with Gemini Code Assist agent mode.
cards.misconception: Gemini CLI has an independent request pool from Code Assist agent mode.
cards.volatilityNote: AI product quotas and edition entitlements can change.

cards.statement: Google Antigravity's visual artifacts can include browser recordings alongside code diffs.
cards.explanation: Google Antigravity uses visual artifacts, including plans, code diffs, and browser recordings, to show and verify agent work.
cards.volatilityNote: Google Antigravity's agent reporting features can change.

cards.statement: Gemini Cloud Assist can refine Terraform infrastructure code through chat prompts.
cards.explanation: Gemini Cloud Assist supports interactive generation and refinement of Terraform code for Google Cloud infrastructure.
cards.volatilityNote: Gemini Cloud Assist is a Preview offering.

cards.statement: By default, gcloud storage cp downloads objects locally before copying between Cloud Storage buckets.
cards.explanation: The default gcloud storage cp mode copies objects in the cloud. Local download followed by upload is the optional daisy-chain mode.
cards.misconception: Cloud Storage bucket-to-bucket copies pass through the command user's machine by default.

cards.statement: Cloud Shell uses the local workstation's gcloud CLI installation.
cards.explanation: Cloud Shell runs in a Google-managed virtual machine with the gcloud CLI preinstalled. Its tool installation is separate from the user's workstation.
cards.misconception: Cloud Shell runs the gcloud CLI installed on the user's computer.

cards.statement: The gcloud compute ssh command opens an SSH connection to a Compute Engine VM.
cards.explanation: The Google Cloud CLI uses gcloud compute ssh to connect to a Compute Engine VM over SSH.

cards.statement: A Compute Engine snapshot schedule automatically creates disk backups on a chosen cadence.
cards.explanation: A Compute Engine snapshot schedule creates snapshots of an attached Persistent Disk or Hyperdisk at its configured intervals.

cards.statement: A Compute Engine machine image stores the source VM's memory state.
cards.explanation: A Compute Engine machine image captures VM configuration and disk data, but not data held in the VM's memory.
cards.misconception: Machine images preserve a running VM's RAM contents.

cards.statement: GKE cluster autoscaling changes the node count of Standard node pools as demand changes.
cards.explanation: In GKE Standard, cluster autoscaling adds or removes VMs in node pools to respond to workload demand.

cards.statement: By default, GKE nodes pull private Artifact Registry images using the deployer's user credentials.
cards.explanation: GKE image pulls use the node's service account and its Artifact Registry access, subject to the node's access scopes. A deployer's login does not authorize the nodes.
cards.misconception: The person deploying a workload supplies the default identity for GKE image pulls.
cards.volatilityNote: Default image-pull access varies with GKE version and node configuration.

cards.statement: GKE Autopilot supplies default resource requests for Pod containers that omit them.
cards.explanation: GKE Autopilot fills in missing Pod container resource requests using defaults for the selected compute configuration.
cards.volatilityNote: GKE Autopilot request defaults can vary by version and compute class.

cards.statement: Manually upgrading a GKE Standard node pool upgrades the cluster's other pools at the same time.
cards.explanation: GKE Standard node pools can be upgraded independently, so a manual upgrade of one pool does not upgrade the other pools.
cards.misconception: A manual GKE node pool upgrade is a cluster-wide node upgrade.

cards.statement: Cloud Run can split service traffic among revisions by percentage.
cards.explanation: Cloud Run traffic settings assign percentages to service revisions, enabling gradual rollouts and rollbacks.

source.title: Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration

cards.statement: A Cloud Run revision's maximum instance setting caps instances across the whole service.
cards.explanation: A Cloud Run revision maximum applies to that revision. When a service splits traffic across revisions, its total instance count can exceed one revision's maximum.
cards.misconception: A revision-level maximum instance setting limits the combined instances of a service.

source.title: About instance autoscaling in Cloud Run services

cards.statement: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform lists deployed agents across an organization.
cards.explanation: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform lists deployed agents for a specified Google Cloud project and location.
cards.misconception: One Agent Runtime listing spans an entire organization.
tags: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
cards.volatilityNote: Agent Runtime management interfaces and product branding can change.

cards.statement: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench opens a JupyterLab notebook environment.
cards.explanation: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench instances provide JupyterLab for notebook-based development.
cards.volatilityNote: Workbench images and product branding can change.

cards.statement: Cloud Workstations retains its runtime VM after a user session ends.
cards.explanation: Cloud Workstations deletes the runtime VM when a session ends. It detaches and retains the persistent home disk for later sessions.
cards.misconception: A stopped workstation keeps its runtime VM for the next session.

cards.statement: Cloud Storage uniform bucket-level access uses IAM for object access instead of ACLs.
cards.explanation: Enabling uniform bucket-level access disables bucket and object ACLs, leaving IAM to grant access to objects in the bucket.

cards.statement: A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule moves an object to a new bucket when changing its storage class.
cards.explanation: A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule's SetStorageClass action changes an eligible object's storage class in its existing bucket.
cards.misconception: A lifecycle storage-class transition transfers the object into a different bucket.

cards.statement: The bq command-line tool submits SQL queries to BigQuery.
cards.explanation: The bq query command creates a BigQuery query job that runs the supplied SQL.

cards.statement: Cloud SQL for MySQL uses binary logs to support point-in-time recovery.
cards.explanation: Cloud SQL for MySQL enables binary logging for point-in-time recovery, allowing restoration to a chosen point within the retained log window.

cards.statement: Firestore backup schedules store backups in a Cloud Storage bucket selected by the user.
cards.explanation: Firestore scheduled backups are managed backup resources that reside in the same location as their source database; the user does not select a Cloud Storage bucket.
cards.misconception: Firestore scheduled backups use a user-chosen Cloud Storage destination.

cards.statement: A Bigtable backup passes through Cloud Storage when restored to a different instance.
cards.explanation: Bigtable restores its managed backups directly into a table, including in a different instance; no Cloud Storage export or import is needed.
cards.misconception: Cross-instance Bigtable recovery needs a Cloud Storage staging step.

cards.statement: The Dataflow monitoring interface shows whether a job is running, completed, or failed.
cards.explanation: The Dataflow monitoring interface lists jobs by status and provides details about their stages, metrics, and logs.

source.title: Use the Dataflow job monitoring interface

cards.statement: Database Center reports real-time health data for a database fleet.
cards.explanation: Database Center summarizes fleet health issues, but its displayed data is not real-time and can take time to update.
cards.misconception: Database Center health findings update instantly with database state.
cards.volatilityNote: Database Center data freshness and dashboard behavior can change.

cards.statement: An early Nearline deletion can incur a charge for the remaining minimum storage duration.
cards.explanation: Cloud Storage may apply an early deletion charge when a Nearline object is deleted before its minimum storage duration ends.

cards.statement: A Cloud Storage regional bucket uses a CMEK key ring in that same region.
cards.explanation: Cloud Storage requires a Cloud KMS key ring used for customer-managed encryption to match the location of the bucket's data.

cards.statement: AlloyDB continuous backup can restore a cluster directly into another region.
cards.explanation: AlloyDB continuous backup creates a recovered cluster in the same region as its source cluster.
cards.misconception: AlloyDB point-in-time recovery directly creates a cluster in a different region.

cards.statement: A Spanner backup keeps its original expiration date after creation.
cards.explanation: Spanner lets an operator update an existing backup's expiration date using the console or gcloud spanner backups update-metadata.
cards.misconception: A Spanner backup's retention endpoint is immutable.
